clue.text: Fixed between the red and green here's a novel heroine

definitions.text: Fixed between the red and green
definitions.meaning: a traffic light stuck for good on the middle colour, between stop and go
Amber St Clare, heroine of Kathleen Winsor's 1944 bestselling novel

explanation.surface: A traffic signal stuck on one colour turns out to be the heroine of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part literally: a traffic light permanently showing its middle colour, which sits between red and green.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Kathleen Winsor's novel is also the name commonly given to its heroine, while the phrase literally describes a signal stuck on one colour.

clue.text: War foes got together and looked ahead prophetically

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are gathered and reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: Old enemies make peace and predict the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got together' rearranges the seven letters of WAR FOES.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict or anticipate events before they happen.

clue.text: Campanologists doubles

definitions.meaning: bell-..., people who ring church bells
lookalikes or substitutes passed off as someone else

explanation.definitionFit: Bell-ringers are campanologists, and a dead ringer is a person's exact lookalike, hence doubles.

clue.text: Extremely short-weight brightener for the battlefield

parts.note: extremely means very
goods sold short-weight are light

explanation.surface: Something of reduced weight lights up a battle scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a flare fired over a battlefield to illuminate or signal.

clue.text: Continue with tears in York shire

parts.note: tears as a verb means rips
on is used as a command meaning carry on or continue

explanation.surface: Weeping goes on somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping but is the verb (to rip). Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city located within the county of Yorkshire.

clue.text: The sound of wonder for poetic Andrew

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word pronounced like another word

parts.note: a wonder is a marvel

explanation.surface: A wondrous noise is linked with a poet called Andrew.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was the seventeenth-century poet of 'To His Coy Mistress'.

clue.text: Mixed diet I add on to form of published work

indicators.note: the letters are blended together and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter's mixed-up menu is turned into a printed volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges DIET and I into EDITI; 'add' tells you to tack ON to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is a particular version or printing in which a book or paper is issued.

clue.text: Traveller's joy: the fringe of senescence

definitions.meaning: the wild clematis, a climbing hedgerow plant
the whiskers grown by an elderly gentleman

explanation.definitionFit: Wild clematis is popularly named for its fluffy grey seed heads, and an elderly man's whiskers are literally his fringe in old age.

clue.text: Liveryman whose work was found in bits

definitions.text: Liveryman whose work was found in bits

parts.words: Liveryman whose work was found in bits
parts.note: a member of a London livery company whose craft was making the metal mouthpieces of horses' bridles

explanation.surface: A guild member's work turned up in fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' sounds like fragments, but means the mouthpieces of bridles; the Worshipful Company of Loriners is a City of London livery company.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner makes spurs, stirrups and bridle bits, and the trade has its own City livery company.

clue.text: Part of statute not quite pure to look at

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to look at is to view

explanation.surface: A clause of law is not entirely clean when examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of PURE to give PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the purview is the enacting body of a statute, setting out its scope.

clue.text: Hip hooray! That's a comforting message!

explanation.definitionFit: A cry of 'hip hip hooray' is literally a cheer put into speech, and the phrase also means encouraging remarks.

clue.text: Cards that wrongly change hands

parts.note: playing cards given out in error by the dealer

explanation.surface: Dodgy cards pass illegitimately from one owner to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change hands' suggests a dishonest sale, but the hands are the sets of cards dealt to players.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is an error in distributing cards, after which the hands must be redealt.

clue.text: Requirement that is right though comparatively poor

parts.note: a requirement is a need

explanation.surface: A need that is justified even though one is poorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, meaning more in want and so poorer.

clue.text: Amphibians went astray southwards

indicators.note: the letters wander off course into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Some amphibians wandered off heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges WENT; S is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are small tailed amphibians related to salamanders.

clue.text: Course that should be studied by conscientious drivers

definitions.text: Course that should be studied by conscientious drivers

parts.words: Course that should be studied by conscientious drivers
parts.note: a sporting ground where golfers who hit tee shots with drivers learn the layout

explanation.surface: A training course that careful motorists ought to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists and 'course' a lesson, but the drivers are golf clubs and the course is where they are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf links are a seaside course, which serious golfers study before playing.

clue.text: Southampton, for example, provides ample after dinner drink

parts.note: ample means large
port is a fortified wine served after dinner

explanation.surface: Southampton generously supplies a digestif.
explanation.walkthrough: Southampton is a major harbour city on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Southampton is a big seaport with extensive docks, an example of a major harbour town.

clue.text: Counsel returning polite form of address in exchange

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: barter is trading by exchange

indicators.note: returning means the courteous title is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a polite way of addressing a man

explanation.surface: A lawyer comes back courteously during a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SIR into RIS, which goes 'in' BARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a counsel is a lawyer who pleads cases in court, a member of the bar.

clue.text: Circular on a round foundation

parts.note: a building that is round in plan and rests on a circular base

explanation.surface: A leaflet sits on a round base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet but describes a round building; ROTUND (round) plus A also lies behind the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, often domed, raised on a round plan.

clue.text: Innings disturbed by a pub hanger-on

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: A cricket innings is interrupted by a drinker hanging around the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges INNINGS. A pub's sign hangs outside it, making it a hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted board hanging outside a tavern is literally a thing that hangs on the pub.

clue.text: Literal finishing stroke back fires

indicators.note: back means the word fires is read from the end to the start

explanation.surface: A last blow comes before the weapons fire again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' means 'of letters' here: a serif is a small stroke ending a letter in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small cross-line finishing off a printed character's stroke.

clue.text: Qualified respect for royal staff

indicators.note: qualified in the sense of modified, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Grudging esteem for the people who work for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal staff' suggests palace employees, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod held by a monarch as a symbol of sovereignty.

clue.text: He takes a practical view about a catalogue

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A pragmatic man browses a brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who sees things as they are and acts practically.

clue.text: Waits as a road race finishes

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle road race on the Isle of Man
finishes means ends

explanation.surface: Someone waits while a motor race comes to its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' as in waits on, serves: to attend upon someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait on someone is to attend them, serving as a servant or helper does.

clue.text: Material designed to be of sedentary use?

definitions.text: Material designed to be of sedentary use?

parts.words: Material designed to be of sedentary use?
parts.note: a fabric whose name, split in two, suggests having been seated in

explanation.surface: A fabric made for people who sit about.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SAT IN and it describes something used while sitting, as the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, and its name splits into a phrase about having been seated.

clue.text: Clean-up for the viewer is vulgar nonsense

definitions.meaning: a lotion for bathing the organ of sight
rubbish or claptrap in colloquial speech

explanation.definitionFit: An eye lotion literally bathes the organ of sight, and colloquially the word means humbug or rubbish.

clue.text: Does he look down in the mouth because he finds his drill boring?

definitions.text: Does he look down in the mouth because he finds his drill boring?

parts.words: Does he look down in the mouth because he finds his drill boring?
parts.note: a professional who peers into patients' mouths and uses a drill that bores into teeth

explanation.surface: Is a man gloomy because his routine bores him?
explanation.walkthrough: 'down in the mouth' means glum and 'boring' means tedious, but literally he looks into mouths and his drill bores teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon examines teeth by looking into the mouth and drilling cavities.

clue.text: Come here to fight

parts.note: the challenge to step out of doors to settle a quarrel with fists

explanation.surface: A belligerent invitation to step up and brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come here' is a location: the challenge 'come ___' invites a rival out of the pub or room for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The challenge to a brawl is to step out of doors, so that place is where one comes to fight.

clue.text: The way in which the City's big guns are assembled?

definitions.text: The way in which the City's big guns are assembled?

parts.words: The way in which the City's big guns are assembled?
parts.note: a road in the financial district imagined as the place where artillery is gathered

explanation.surface: How the leading financiers of London get together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big guns' suggests important City people, but here they are artillery pieces; 'way' is a road. CANNON STREET is a street and station in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This thoroughfare in London's financial district has a name made of heavy guns and a road.
